accepted.s: Samvidhan Divas has been observed in India since which year?
accepted.x: Samvidhan Divas has been observed since 2015, the year of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar's 125th birth anniversary.
accepted.tq: Use the precise year rather than confusing the observance with Constitution adoption.
accepted.sec: Remarks by framers and Constitution Day

accepted.s: On 24 January 1950, which song was declared the national song of India and accorded equal honour with the National Anthem?
accepted.x: Rajendra Prasad declared Vande Mataram the national song on 24 January 1950 and stated that it would be honoured equally with the National Anthem.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the national song from the National Anthem.
accepted.sec: Remarks by framers and Constitution Day

accepted.s: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar warned against the “grammar of anarchy” in his closing speech delivered on:
accepted.x: Ambedkar used the expression “grammar of anarchy” in his closing speech on 25 November 1949.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between closely related Constitution-making dates.
accepted.sec: Remarks by framers and Constitution Day

accepted.s: Who stated that constitutional morality “is not a natural sentiment. It has to be cultivated”?
accepted.x: The statement was made by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar on 4 November 1948. The expression was borrowed from George Grote.
accepted.tq: Match a distinctive quotation with its speaker.
accepted.sec: Remarks by framers and Constitution Day

accepted.s: The expression “Drifting Committee”, referring to the alleged slowness of the Drafting Committee, was used by:
accepted.x: Naziruddin Ahmed criticised the pace of the Drafting Committee by calling it a “Drifting Committee”.
accepted.tq: Use the quotation-speaker association as the identifying clue.
accepted.sec: Criticisms of the Assembly - representativeness, composition, time taken

accepted.s: Who described the Constituent Assembly as “a one-party body in an essentially one-party country”?
accepted.x: Granville Austin described the Assembly in these terms, highlighting its Congress dominance.
accepted.tq: Identify the critic associated with a political characterisation.
accepted.sec: Criticisms of the Assembly - representativeness, composition, time taken

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about criticisms of the Constituent Assembly:
1. It was criticised for not being based on adult franchise.
2. It was criticised as not sovereign because it originated from British proposals.
3. It was criticised for taking about three years to complete its work.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The Assembly lacked a direct adult-franchise basis, originated under British proposals, and took about three years.
accepted.tq: Combine institutional criticism, origin and time-related statements.
accepted.sec: Criticisms of the Assembly - representativeness, composition, time taken

accepted.s: The Constituent Assembly took approximately how long to frame the Constitution, as compared with about four months taken by the United States?
accepted.x: The Assembly took about three years, whereas the United States is stated to have taken about four months.
accepted.tq: Use the comparative time figure rather than an isolated duration.
accepted.sec: Criticisms of the Assembly - representativeness, composition, time taken

accepted.s: Who described the Constituent Assembly as “a body of Hindus”?
accepted.x: Viscount Simon used the phrase “a body of Hindus” while criticising the composition of the Assembly.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between similar criticisms by their speakers.
accepted.sec: Criticisms of the Assembly - representativeness, composition, time taken

accepted.s: The Constituent Assembly was criticised for representing “only one major community” by:
accepted.x: Winston Churchill made the criticism that the Assembly represented “only one major community”.
accepted.tq: Match the exact wording of a criticism with its author.
accepted.sec: Criticisms of the Assembly - representativeness, composition, time taken

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT a criticism directed against the Constituent Assembly?
o: It was a British-created body and therefore not sovereign.
It was dominated by lawyers and politicians.
It was based on universal adult franchise.
accepted.x: The Assembly was criticised precisely because it was not based on adult franchise. The other three were recognised criticisms.
accepted.tq: Find the option that reverses a known criticism.
accepted.sec: Criticisms of the Assembly - representativeness, composition, time taken

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes India's status on 15 August 1947?
o: A sovereign republic with no constitutional link to the Crown
A federation of independent princely states
A Dominion with the British monarch as nominal head
A colony governed directly by the British Parliament
accepted.x: India became a Dominion on 15 August 1947, with the British monarch as its nominal head.
accepted.tq: Separate Dominion status from republican status.
accepted.sec: British Crown's residual role - Governor-General, dominion status

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Governor-General after independence:
1. The same Governor-General could, in principle, be appointed for both Dominions.
2. Each Dominion could have its own Governor-General.
3. The Governor-General was to act on the advice of the Dominion ministers.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The arrangement permitted one common Governor-General or separate Governors-General, who were to act on ministerial advice.
accepted.tq: Test several linked features of a constitutional office.
accepted.sec: British Crown's residual role - Governor-General, dominion status

accepted.s: Who was the last and only Indian Governor-General of India?
accepted.x: C. Rajagopalachari served as Governor-General from June 1948 to January 1950 and was the last and only Indian to hold the office.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the first office-holder from the last and only Indian office-holder.
accepted.sec: British Crown's residual role - Governor-General, dominion status

accepted.s:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
A. India became a Republic
B. Lord Mountbatten became Governor-General of free India
C. C. Rajagopalachari became Governor-General
D. India became a Dominion
accepted.x: Mountbatten became Governor-General in 1947, India became a Dominion on 15 August 1947, Rajagopalachari assumed office in June 1948, and India became a Republic on 26 January 1950.
accepted.tq: Fix the first and last events before ordering the middle events.
accepted.sec: British Crown's residual role - Governor-General, dominion status

accepted.s: Dominion status of India ended when India became a Republic on:
accepted.x: India's Dominion status ended on 26 January 1950, when the Constitution came into force and India became a Republic.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the adoption date from the commencement date.
accepted.sec: British Crown's residual role - Governor-General, dominion status

accepted.s: The first law in independent India to receive the assent of the Governor-General was the:
accepted.x: C. Rajagopalachari assented to the Madras Estates (Abolition) Act on 2 April 1949, making it the first such law.
accepted.tq: Match the office-holder, law and date without confusing the constitutional statutes.
accepted.sec: British Crown's residual role - Governor-General, dominion status

accepted.s: The Mountbatten Plan was announced on:
accepted.x: The Mountbatten Plan, also known as the 3 June Plan, was announced on 3 June 1947.
accepted.tq: Use the alternative name of the plan as a date cue.
accepted.sec: Mountbatten Plan (3 June Plan) - partition procedure and provinces voting

accepted.s: Who proposed immediate transfer of power on Dominion status without waiting for a new Constitution?
accepted.x: V.P. Menon proposed immediate transfer of power on Dominion status rather than waiting for a new Constitution.
accepted.tq: Identify the person associated with the specific procedural proposal.
accepted.sec: Mountbatten Plan (3 June Plan) - partition procedure and provinces voting

accepted.s:
With reference to the partition procedure under the Mountbatten Plan, consider the following statements:
1. The Punjab and Bengal Assemblies met in separate sections representing Muslim-majority and Hindu-majority districts.
2. A simple majority in either section was sufficient for partition of the province.
3. Both Punjab and Bengal voted for partition.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The two provincial Assemblies met in separate sections, and a simple majority in either section led to partition; both provinces voted for partition.
accepted.tq: Test the voting mechanism and its result together.
accepted.sec: Mountbatten Plan (3 June Plan) - partition procedure and provinces voting

accepted.s: Which province decided its future separately under the Mountbatten Plan rather than through the Punjab-Bengal sectional procedure?
accepted.x: Sindh decided its future separately under the Mountbatten Plan.
accepted.tq: Separate the individually deciding province from the provinces using sectional voting.
accepted.sec: Mountbatten Plan (3 June Plan) - partition procedure and provinces voting

accepted.s: Which pair of regions was associated with referendums under the Mountbatten Plan?
accepted.x: Referendums were held in the North-West Frontier Province and Sylhet. NWFP joined Pakistan, while Sylhet, a district of Assam, joined East Pakistan.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure pair of regions decided by referendum.
accepted.sec: Mountbatten Plan (3 June Plan) - partition procedure and provinces voting

accepted.s: Which statement regarding the referendum in the North-West Frontier Province is correct?
o: It resulted in the province joining India after a Congress-led campaign.
It was replaced by a vote of the Bengal Assembly.
It resulted in the province becoming an independent state.
It was boycotted by the Khudai Khidmatgar movement, but the province joined Pakistan.
accepted.x: The Khudai Khidmatgar movement boycotted the referendum, but the North-West Frontier Province joined Pakistan.
accepted.tq: Use the outcome and boycott detail to reject reversed alternatives.
accepted.sec: Mountbatten Plan (3 June Plan) - partition procedure and provinces voting

accepted.s: The Radcliffe Boundary Commission was established primarily to:
o: divide the civil services between India and Pakistan
fix the boundaries between the new Dominions
accepted.x: The Boundary Commission was appointed to fix the borders between India and Pakistan.
accepted.tq: Match the commission with its precise function.
accepted.sec: Mountbatten Plan (3 June Plan) - partition procedure and provinces voting

accepted.s: The transfer of power under the Mountbatten Plan was carried out on the basis of the:
accepted.x: Power was transferred on the basis of the Government of India Act, 1935, while the armed forces were also divided.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the operative administrative statute from the later independence statute.
accepted.sec: Mountbatten Plan (3 June Plan) - partition procedure and provinces voting

accepted.s: The proposal that provinces could become independent successor states, later rejected by Jawaharlal Nehru as leading to Balkanisation, was known as the:
accepted.x: The Dickie Bird Plan proposed independent successor states for the provinces and was rejected by Nehru as a plan for Balkanisation.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between similarly named constitutional and partition plans.
accepted.sec: Mountbatten Plan (3 June Plan) - partition procedure and provinces voting

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT a provision of the Indian Independence Act, 1947?
o: Lapse of British paramountcy over princely states
Continuation of the office of the Viceroy as the constitutional head of both Dominions
Abolition of the office of the Secretary of State for India
Creation of two Dominions, India and Pakistan
accepted.x: The Act abolished the office of the Viceroy; each Dominion was to have a Governor-General. The other three were provisions of the Act.
accepted.tq: Find the option that reverses an abolition provision.
accepted.sec: Main provisions of the Act - dominions, paramountcy, Constituent Assembly

accepted.s: Under the Indian Independence Act, 1947, the two Dominions were free to:
o: retain the British veto over all legislation
continue British paramountcy over princely states
accepted.x: India and Pakistan were created as Dominions from 15 August 1947 and were free to leave the Commonwealth.
accepted.tq: Test the scope of Dominion freedom against residual Crown powers.
accepted.sec: Main provisions of the Act - dominions, paramountcy, Constituent Assembly

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Constituent Assemblies under the Indian Independence Act, 1947:
1. They were given sovereign power to frame any Constitution.
2. They could repeal any British law, including the Indian Independence Act itself.
3. They were required to retain all British laws permanently.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Constituent Assemblies had sovereign constitutional authority; they were not required to retain British laws permanently.
accepted.tq: Spot the absolute reversal in the statement containing “permanently”.
accepted.sec: Main provisions of the Act - dominions, paramountcy, Constituent Assembly

accepted.s: Until a new Constitution was framed, each Dominion was governed under the:
o: Government of India Act, 1935, as adapted
Government of India Act, 1919, without alteration
accepted.x: The interim law for each Dominion was the Government of India Act, 1935, as adapted, until its new Constitution came into force.
accepted.tq: Identify the interim constitutional framework and its qualification.
accepted.sec: Main provisions of the Act - dominions, paramountcy, Constituent Assembly

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly states the effect of the Indian Independence Act, 1947, on the Crown?
o: The Crown retained a veto over Dominion bills and retained the title Emperor of India.
The Crown became the elected head of both Dominions.
The Crown retained paramountcy over princely states but lost control over civil services.
The Crown lost its veto over Dominion bills and the title Emperor of India was dropped.
accepted.x: The Act removed the Crown's veto over Dominion bills and dropped the title “Emperor of India”.
accepted.tq: Pair two related changes to avoid accepting a partly reversed option.
accepted.sec: Main provisions of the Act - dominions, paramountcy, Constituent Assembly

accepted.s: Which of the following services-related changes was made by the Indian Independence Act, 1947?
o: Recruitment was transferred exclusively to the Governor-General.
The Constituent Assembly was barred from altering civil-service arrangements.
All civil servants were appointed by the British Crown.
Recruitment by the Secretary of State for India was discontinued.
accepted.x: The Act discontinued recruitment by the Secretary of State for India.
accepted.tq: Identify the correct authority-related change rather than a substituted office-holder.
accepted.sec: Main provisions of the Act - dominions, paramountcy, Constituent Assembly

accepted.s: The lapse of paramountcy in 1947 meant that:
o: The princely states automatically became part of India.
British suzerainty over the princely states ended.
The princely states were placed under the United Nations.
The British monarch became the constitutional ruler of every princely state.
accepted.x: Paramountcy lapsed, ending British suzerainty over the princely states. It did not automatically incorporate them into India.
accepted.tq: Apply the legal consequence of lapse of paramountcy without assuming automatic merger.
accepted.sec: Princely states - options, Instrument of Accession, Standstill Agreement

accepted.s: Approximately how many princely states were theoretically free after the lapse of paramountcy?
accepted.x: About 565 princely states were theoretically free after paramountcy lapsed, although in practice they were expected to join India or Pakistan.
accepted.tq: Use the stated approximate figure and reject adjacent-number traps.
accepted.sec: Princely states - options, Instrument of Accession, Standstill Agreement

accepted.s: Which of the following subjects were ceded to a Dominion by a princely state through an Instrument of Accession?
accepted.x: An Instrument of Accession transferred defence, external affairs and communications to the concerned Dominion.
accepted.tq: Recall the standard three-subject grouping in the accession instrument.
accepted.sec: Princely states - options, Instrument of Accession, Standstill Agreement

accepted.s: The principal purpose of a Standstill Agreement was to:
o: permit a state to declare permanent neutrality
transfer all sovereign powers of a princely state to India
continue existing administrative arrangements until final terms were settled
abolish communications between a state and the Dominion
accepted.x: A Standstill Agreement continued existing administrative arrangements with the Dominion until final terms were settled.
accepted.tq: Distinguish temporary administrative continuity from transfer of sovereignty.
accepted.sec: Princely states - options, Instrument of Accession, Standstill Agreement

accepted.s: Which princely state signed a Standstill Agreement in November 1947?
accepted.x: Hyderabad signed a Standstill Agreement in November 1947.
accepted.tq: Match the state with the specific agreement and time reference.
accepted.sec: Princely states - options, Instrument of Accession, Standstill Agreement

accepted.s: Kashmir acceded to India on:
accepted.x: Kashmir acceded to India on 26 October 1947 after the tribal invasion.
accepted.tq: Separate the accession date from the later ceasefire date.
accepted.sec: Princely states - options, Instrument of Accession, Standstill Agreement

accepted.s: The UN-arranged ceasefire relating to Kashmir came into effect on:
accepted.x: The UN-arranged ceasefire came into effect on 1 January 1949, after Kashmir's accession on 26 October 1947.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the accession event and the subsequent ceasefire.
accepted.sec: Princely states - options, Instrument of Accession, Standstill Agreement
